My pick is the VIOFO A119M Pro if you want the best front-facing 4K footage under $200. It records native 4K at 30 fps with HDR, uses Sony’s excellent STARVIS 2 IMX678 sensor, and has a supercapacitor rather than a lithium battery. Its main limitation is that you cannot add a rear camera.

If you want front-and-rear coverage, I’d choose the 70mai A810S instead.

What I’d actually buy

For a strict $200 total budget, look for the VIOFO around $130–$160 and use the remaining money for a compatible high-endurance microSD card. A November 19 price check found it at $132.99, although the retailer feed currently shows a higher price.

I prioritized native 4K image quality over camera count because you didn't specify whether you need rear coverage. No dash cam can guarantee readable plates at night, particularly in rain or when vehicles are moving quickly. Parking recording also generally requires a separately purchased hardwire kit. What matters more than the 4K label

Look for HDR and a good sensor, especially for nighttime license plates. Even these cameras cannot reliably capture every moving plate in darkness or glare. Budget for a compatible high-endurance microSD card, and remember that parking surveillance generally requires a separate hardwire kit. 
RoadGearLab

Bottom line: Get the VIOFO if front-video detail matters most; get the 70mai dual bundle if you want broader accident coverage.
